sections.h2: What should a seller know about Arizona before opening a county or city guide?
sections.html:
Arizona is large, thinly privately owned and split into 15 counties, so the rules that touch a house sale come mostly from state law while the practical details change by county. The state covers 113,998 square miles, and only about 15 percent of that is privately owned. The rest is public forest and parkland, state trust land and Native American reservations.

The state became the 48th state on February 14, 1912. Phoenix is both the capital and the largest city, and Maricopa is the largest county. The 2020 census counted 7,151,502 residents, a 12 percent rise over 2010. Maricopa and Pima are the two biggest counties, so many of the guides below start there.

For a seller, three questions come first. Which county recorder will record the deed? Which county assessor and treasurer handle the tax bill? And is the lot on private land at all, since about one quarter of the state is Indian reservation land with 27 federally recognized tribes? A parcel on trust or reservation land follows different title rules, so ask the county or a title company before assuming a normal sale.

sections.h2: How many counties does Arizona have, and how do they compare?
sections.html:
Arizona has 15 counties, and they differ enormously in size. Coconino County is the largest by area at 18,661 square miles, while Santa Cruz County is the smallest at 1,238. Greenlee County has the fewest residents and Maricopa County has the most by a wide margin.

Counties here have no home-rule charters. They are legal creatures of the state and are run by boards of supervisors under state statute, which is one reason the property tax calendar and recording rules look alike across the state even though each county has its own offices.

sections.h2: How do Arizona's regions differ for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Where the house sits changes the climate it has to survive, the buyer pool and the county office you deal with. A rough split into regions helps.

  • Phoenix metro (Maricopa County and the western edge of Pinal County). Cities such as Tempe at 184,118 people and Surprise at 149,191 are among the state's largest, according to the Wikipedia city list. Casa Grande in Pinal County has 57,699.
  • Tucson and the south (Pima, Santa Cruz, Cochise). Tucson was founded as a Spanish presidio in 1775, and Tubac in 1752. Marana, in Pima County, is listed at 54,895.
  • The high country (Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, Apache). Flagstaff sits at nearly 7,000 feet in ponderosa pine forest. Prescott lies near 5,500 feet, and Yavapai County's metro area, with 212,635 residents, is the third largest in the state.
  • The Colorado River side (Mohave, La Paz, Yuma). Yuma's metro area has about 160,000 residents and draws many winter visitors. Lake Havasu City in Mohave County is listed at 58,284.

Ask the county office for local requirements before listing, because city and county rules on permits and code enforcement are set locally and are not covered by the state statutes cited on this page.

sections.h2: How does Arizona's climate affect an older house?
sections.html:
The lower elevations are desert with mild winters and extremely hot summers, while the north has snow, so the same year can stress a house in opposite ways depending on where it stands. Elevation runs from 72 feet at the Colorado River on the Mexican border to 12,638 feet at Humphreys Peak.

In the desert, summers are extremely hot, which is hard on roofs and cooling equipment. A late summer monsoon, usually in July or August, brings lightning, wind and heavy downpours after a brief rise in humidity. Roof leaks, drainage problems and storm damage tend to show up after those storms.

In the northern forests, snow loads and freezing temperatures matter more. A house with deferred work on the roof, cooling system or plumbing is one where owners often weigh repairing first against selling as-is.

sections.h2: How is property tax billed across the state?
sections.html:
Arizona runs property tax on one statewide calendar: half the bill is due October 1 and the other half the following March 1. The first half becomes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. If a delinquency date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to 5:00 p.m. on the next business day. A bill of $100 or less is due in full on October 1 and is delinquent after December 31.

Owners who think the county assessor valued the property too high can file a petition with the assessor on a form prescribed by the Department of Revenue. The petition is due within 60 days after the assessor mailed the notice of valuation, and it must state the owner's opinion of full cash value with supporting information such as a comparable property or the sale price.

These dates apply in every county. What changes is where you pay and which office answers questions, so confirm with the county treasurer and assessor for your parcel.

  • First half due October 1, delinquent after November 1.
  • Second half due March 1, delinquent after May 1.
  • Valuation petition: 60 days from the mailing date of the notice.

sections.h2: What paperwork does an Arizona deed need when it is recorded?
sections.html:
Every deed that transfers title, and any contract for the sale of real property, must have an affidavit of legal value attached when it is recorded. The seller and buyer, or an agent for either, jointly certify it on a Department of Revenue form, and the county recorder will refuse to record the deed if the affidavit is incomplete.

The affidavit asks for names and mailing addresses, the legal description, the situs address, the date of sale, the total price and down payment, the type of financing, the assessor's parcel number, and whether a residence will be owner occupied or rented. It also asks whether personal property worth five percent or more of the price changed hands.

Some transfers skip the affidavit, and the deed must say which exemption applies. Examples in the statute include a deed of gift, a quitclaim executed for no money, a court-ordered conveyance, a trustee's deed under a deed of trust, transfers for only nominal consideration between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren or siblings, and a transfer under a beneficiary deed with nominal consideration.

sections.h2: Which Arizona topics usually come up when a house must sell quickly?
sections.html:
Sellers in a hurry tend to run into the same short list of statewide topics, each covered in its own guide on this site.

  • Probate. An heir who wants to sell must first learn whether a personal representative has authority or whether an affidavit route applies.
  • Homestead protection. It shields a primary residence from most judgment creditors but not from a mortgage or certain other liens.
  • Rentals with tenants. A lease and a security deposit do not disappear when the house sells.
  • Tax bills and liens. A delinquent tax balance is worth checking early with the county treasurer.

Each of these has its own deadlines under Arizona statute. When a question involves a court filing, a lien payoff or a lease dispute, an attorney or title company should confirm the final steps.

faqs.q: How many counties are in Arizona?
faqs.a: Arizona has 15 counties. Maricopa is the largest by population, Coconino is the largest by area, and La Paz, created in 1983, is the newest.

faqs.q: When are Arizona property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due October 1 and half is due March 1. Unpaid first-half taxes become delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, and unpaid second-half taxes after 5:00 p.m. on May 1.

faqs.q: Does every Arizona deed need an affidavit of legal value?
faqs.a: Most do. The county recorder must refuse a deed without a complete affidavit unless the deed notes a listed exemption, such as a deed of gift or a trustee's deed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house on tribal land in Arizona like any other house?
faqs.a: Not always. About one quarter of Arizona is Indian reservation land, and title on those parcels follows different rules, so ask the county recorder or a title company before agreeing to a sale.

faqs.q: Who runs county government in Arizona?
faqs.a: Each county is run by a board of supervisors under state law. Counties have no home-rule charters, so their powers come from the state legislature.
